title: AI-Powered Hacker Operation Scans 726,000 Hosts and Harvests 16,834 Credentials
content_md: A French-speaking cybercrime group allegedly used an AI-enabled attack platform to scan nearly 727,000 internet-facing hosts and collect 16,834 credentials from exposed files and weak configurations. Security researchers discovered an exposed operation server linked to the group known as BlackHatSect0r && DXQRTXX. The server reportedly contained 4.9 GB of data across 9,299 files, including a custom command-and-control platform, stolen credential vaults, phishing tools, extortion material, and AI-agent configuration files. The group’s main platform, called DXSCAN, was written in Go and operated as a large-scale scanning system. Researchers said the platform queued 2,759,860 domains, reached 726,989 hosts, and generated more than 1.37 million IP addresses during the operation. AI Hacker Harvests 16,834 Credentials The scanner checked systems on common web ports, including 80, 443, and 8080. It looked for exposed .env files, cloud keys, database credentials, SMTP accounts, API tokens, Git files, and application configuration data. The credential vault reportedly contained 16,834 entries. These included 5,109 generic secrets, 3,448 database credentials, 1,535 SMTP accounts, 936 API keys , 478 AWS keys, 343 GitHub credentials, and 68 Stripe keys. Researchers also found that some SMTP accounts were tested and prepared for possible use in phishing activity. The operation did not rely mainly on unknown vulnerabilities or advanced zero-days.
